newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight interbank rate ends at 6.50 pct.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight interbank rate ends at 6.50 pct.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate closed on Friday at 6.50 percent as borrowing by some large banks kept the rate steady, dealers said.
The overnight rate shot up to 8.7 percent on Wednesday due to borrowing by big banks in late trading, after mostly trading at 5.8/6.0 percent.
The market was closed on Thursday for Labour Day.
"Some banks could be short of funds. They are borrowing back from the market," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
Earlier, interbank rates were generally steady due to lack of lenders in the market, dealers said.
One-week and two-week money were at 6.5/7.0 percent and three-week at 7.10/20 percent, all unchanged from Wednesday.
One-month money was at 7.25/30 percent against 7.20/25, three-month at 7.30/35 percent from 7.25/30 and six-month at 7.35/40 percent against 7.30/35.

But rates could come under pressure again following maturity of a 500 million ringgit Bank Negara bills issue on Friday which would improve liquidity further, dealers said. A 420 million ringgit long-term government bond issue had matured on Wednesday.
But at current levels, further falls are likely to be limited, said another local bank dealer.
Dealers said Bank Negara, to maintain a tight monetary policy, could intervene in the interbank market if rates were to fall sharply.

There have been rumours that the central bank will announce a fresh long-term government bond issue to roll over maturing issues. Another 900 million ringgit worth of Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) will mature on May 15.
"Bank Negara has to do something to mop up the excess funds," one dealer said.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were unchanged to marginally lower.
At 0900 GMT, the benchmark three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June contract was unchanged at 92.68, or an implied yield of 7.32 percent.
September and December were down one point at 92.67 and 92.66, or 7.33 and 7.34 percent respectively.
